title: Eastern P02 radiocarbon loss on density 26.5 exceeds local decay and carbon dilution in 2004-2022
abstract: We test carbon isotopes as a new constraint on North Pacific oxygen loss. We use joint good-flag oxygen, dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) and radiocarbon from P02 in 2004, 2013 and 2022. Four matched longitude bins at 28-32 N and density sigma0 26.5 in the eastern section show a 29.59 per mil radiocarbon fall in 2004-2022, an oxygen loss of 7.65 umol/kg and a DIC gain of 20.01 umol/kg. Local decay gives only 2.18 per mil of the isotope fall. Even if all net added carbon has no radiocarbon, decay and dilution give at most 11.40 per mil. The measured fall would need 60.62 umol/kg of such addition. A joint stable-isotope check retains the isotope-content deficit. An added test on seven common eastern longitude bins finds a 28.94 per mil fall in the 26.5-minus-27.0 isotope contrast. A uniform additive cruise isotope offset cancels in this contrast. The planned western and central tests lack common support, and stricter interpolation cannot give a regional interval near 26.5. These are fixed-density concentration changes, not basin stocks or ventilation-age changes. Transport of the changing bomb-carbon source signal can give an open isotope budget under unchanged flow. The result supplies a new model target but does not select the cause of the oxygen loss. Code, aggregate evidence, exact source hashes, numerical audits and a retrieval recipe are included.

display.caption: Eastern P02 density 26.5: local decay and even radiocarbon-free carbon addition are too small to explain the observed isotope fall. Error bars are conditional spatial intervals. The systematic-error box is a scenario on epoch means. The result requires an open DIC isotope budget, not a ventilation-age change.

Changes by density on the eastern P02 section in 2004-2022. Solid points use the planned interpolation gaps; open points have fewer than four bins. Dashed lines use wider gaps as an exploratory check. Spatial support differs by density; a separate seven-bin vertical control is reported in the text.
